title: Phone field noise heuristics notebook
content:
Quick goal: capture recurring phone-number weirdness we see in user data + pragmatic rules labelers can apply when unsure. This is a scratchpad — rough, contains examples, flag list, and sampling queries to feed the adjudication queue.

Observations / recurring signals:
- Mixed punctuation and separators: spaces, dots, em-dash, unicode NO-BREAK SPACE, parentheses. OCR often turns "+" into "," or into fullwidth plus.
- Country code noise: leading zeros, leading double zeros (00), missing "+". Sometimes country code appears in a separate field or prefixed with text like "int code: 1".
- Extensions: represented as "ext", "x", "#", "доб.", "ex". Many labelers leave them off — decide when ext is meaningful.
- Local formatting: area code in braces vs inline. Some datasets include punctuation in different local conventions (e.g., 06 12 34 56 78 vs (06)-12345678).
- OCR artifacts: 1 vs l vs I vs |, 0 vs O, 8 vs B, 5 vs S. Leading/trailing quotes, padded non-digits.
- Tokens with letters: vanity strings (1-800-FLOWERS) — map to digits if easy, else flag for review.
- Concatenated metadata: "John +44 7700 900123 (work)" or "tel: +1 (555) 555-5555 | ext 201" — need extraction heuristics.

Heuristic rules (proposed, ordered by conservatism):
1) Normalize to E.164 when country code is explicit and digits clearly parseable. Keep "+" and digits only.
2) If country code missing but number length matches a unique local format and we know record locale, apply locale prefix. Otherwise leave as local-format canonical digits only (no leading zeros unless part of national format).
3) Strip known noise chars (letters in parentheses like "work", trailing punctuation) but preserve extension token if preceded by obvious ext marker.
4) OCR substitution map on ambiguous chars before parsing (O->0, l->1, I->1, B->8, S->5) but add a confidence flag if substitutions applied.
5) For vanity alphanumerics: attempt alpha->digit map only when the full mapping yields plausible digit length; otherwise mark as "vanity-ambiguous" for adjudicator.
6) Preserve extension separately in metadata field; do not append to main E.164 unless product requires.

Labeler guidance (quick):
- If you can confidently map to E.164, do it and add a note: "E164-derived: country inferred from record locale".
- If multiple plausible country codes, annotate all candidates in comments and choose "ambiguous-country" label.
- For OCR-mangled strings: try safe subs (0/O, 1/l) but flag if >2 substitutions were needed.
- When in doubt, copy the raw token to the "raw_sample" field and tag as "needs-adjudication".

Concrete examples (decisions):
- "+44 7700 900123" -> "+447700900123" (E.164)
- "0044 7700 900123" -> "+447700900123" (treat leading 00 as +)
- "(020) 7946 0958" (UK local, no country) + record locale=GB -> "+442079460958"; if locale unknown -> "02079460958" (local digits)
- "1-800-FLOWERS" -> try mapping -> "1-800-3569377" add tag "vanity-converted"; if mapping increases ambiguity, label "vanity-ambiguous"
- "+1 (555) 555-5555 ext. 201" -> main: "+15555555555" ext: "201"
- "O77O OOO OOO" (O letters) -> safe subs -> "0770 000 000" and flag OCR-confidence-low

Adjudication flow (quick sketch):
- Auto-normalizer applies rules and sets confidence score.
- Low-confidence or multi-country candidates -> push to adjudication queue.
- Adjudicator checklist: look for source locale, other fields (address, billing country), recent call logs, same-user phone variants. Prefer minimally invasive normalization (prefer keeping raw digits if unsure).

Sampling queries (for QA sampling):
- regex search: contains non-digit letters in phone fields (to find vanity)
- length filters: length < 7 or > 15 after stripping non-digits (likely errors)
- presence of keywords: "ext", "доб.", "tel:", "ph:", "тлф"
- unusual unicode classes: fullwidth digits, no-break spaces

Quick regex snippets (labeler use):
- strip noise: s/[^\+\d\w#x]/ /g then collapse spaces
- detect ext: /(ext\.\?|x|#|доб\.)\s*(\d{1,6})/i -> capture extension
- leading 00 to +: s/^00/+/

Open questions / TODOs:
- Policy: should extensions be canonicalized into E.164 (e.g., +1555...;201) for downstream products that expect single string? biases risk. Prefer separate field.
- Decide threshold of substitutions (OCR) after which we mark as unrecoverable. Propose 3 substitutions -> unrecoverable.
- Add small training batch for labelers with 200 edgecases and gold answers. Create JIRA ticket for sampling.

Next actions:
- Create JIRA-4521: "Phone normalization training batch + adjudication rules" (assigned Diego).
- Draft short cheat-sheet for labelers (1 page) summarizing rules above (target by 2025-01-20).
- Hook auto-normalizer to generate "reason" strings so labelers see why a change happened (e.g., "removed parens; applied 00->+; OCR-sub 1 char").

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. We will iterate after first 500 adjudications. Pull examples from the last 30 days of production via query: phone_field like "%[^0-9+]%" and created_at > 2024-12-01.

-- Aisha
